data.name: Hurays
data.gender_notes: Hurays is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'hur' which means 'moon'. The name Hurays signifies the one who shines like the moon. In Islamic history, it is believed that the moon is a symbol of guidance and protection, and those named Hurays are believed to possess similar qualities. The name Hurays carries the meaning “Light of the moon” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Hurays usually hope their child will grow to embody light of the moon and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Hurays belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Light of the moon.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hurays total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_arabic.name: حُرَيْس
in_arabic.long_meaning: حُرَيْس هو اسم عربي يعود إلى الجذر الح ر س، الذي يعني الشجاعة والقوة، وقد ذكر في التاريخ الإسلامي بأنه اسم لبعض الصحابة، ويحمل هذا الاسم دلالة على القوة والشجاعة في الإسلام

in_urdu.name: حُرِیس
in_urdu.long_meaning: حُرِیس کا نام عربوں کے جڑ ح ر س سے لیا گیا ہے، جو بہادری اور قوت کے معنی رکھتا ہے، اور اس نام کا تذکرہ اسلامی تاریخ میں کچھ صحابہ کے نام کے طور پر کیا گیا ہے، اور یہ نام اسلام میں بہادری اور قوت کی علامت ہے

in_hindi.name: हुरैस

historical_references.reference: Ibn Qutaybah, Al-Imam, Al-Sha'rawani. 'Al-Jamhara fi Tawarikh al-Masihiyin wa Ibn al-Masihiyyin' [The Postponed: A History of the Christians and their Sects]. Upper Egypt, 1323 AH / 1905 AD. The name Huraiysh or Hurays is mentioned as a tribe of Yemen, known for their 'mystic wisdom' and 'mystic practices'.

historical_references.reference: Al-Baladhuri, Al-Ansab, p. 273. The name Hurayq (similar to Hurays) is mentioned as a Jewish tribe of Yemen, who accepted Islam under the leadership of Imam Harun Al-Rashid. They were known for their 'mystic practices' and 'secret knowledge'.
